title: Compatibility Hypothesis Tester for Multimode Rollouts
creator: Omar Singh
description: Build a hypothesis-driven testing harness that simulates environment-specific constraints and traffic patterns to validate canary/A-B/shadow rollouts and auto-rollback policies across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The tool (Compatibility Hypothesis Tester, CHT) will produce a delta-compatibility report highlighting config mismatches, performance regressions, and safety violations before running real customer traffic.
background: We frequently see subtle differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments: networking timeouts, KMS latency, capacity masks, kernel availability, and agent telemetry differences. These cause canaries to behave differently and occasionally trigger false positives/negatives in our rollback logic. Current rollout tests run only in Hosted or require ad-hoc private lab setups. We need an automated simulator that encodes environment hypotheses and verifies rollout policies against them.
proposal: Implement CHT as a pluggable orchestration stage that: 1) accepts a candidate deployment manifest + rollout policy, 2) instantiates synthetic tenant profiles and capacity masks representing Hosted/Dedicated/Private constraints, 3) replays traffic (canary, A/B, and shadow modes) through an isolated runner, 4) evaluates outcome against SLO/metric thresholds and policy predicates, and 5) emits a machine-readable delta-compatibility report and suggested mitigations (config translation hints, fallback routes, or stricter rollback thresholds). The runner must be able to execute fast approximations (low-fidelity, quick) or slower high-fidelity runs that connect to customer-like telemetry collectors.
tasks: Design CHT architecture and data model (manifest, hypothesis templates, runner interface) - RFC
Implement synthetic tenant profile generator (traffic mix, sequence length distribution, KV reuse patterns)
Add capacity mask simulation (GPU count, queue depth, kernel availability) and failure injection (RPC timeouts, KMS delays)
Create replay runner that supports canary, A/B, and shadow modes with configurable sampling rates
Integrate policy checker to evaluate rollout predicates and simulate auto-rollback triggers
Produce delta-compatibility report format and human-friendly remediation suggestions
Wire CHT into Console UI as a pre-rollout validation step and add CLI integration for private labs
Add telemetry adapters for environments with limited metrics (agent-based collection for Private)
Write end-to-end tests and a benchmark harness (fast vs. fidelity sweeps)
Security review and adversarial test cases for Private deployments
acceptance_criteria: CHT RFC merged and architecture reviewed by runtime and infra leads
CHT can simulate at least three hypothesis templates (hosted-default, dedicated-constrained, private-sanctum)
Runner executes a canary replay and produces a delta-compatibility report within configurable time budgets (fast mode < 10m, fidelity mode < 2h)
Policy checker correctly flags rollout violations in simulated Dedicated/Private hypotheses (tested against 5 known past incidents)
Console shows pre-rollout validation pass/fail with link to report; CLI returns machine-readable status code for pipelines
Security review completed and allowed data collection patterns documented for private (agent-only) mode
progress_updates: 2025-07-11: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and console teams. Agreed on three canonical hypothesis templates and minimum report fields (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token-cost delta, rollback flag reasons).
2025-07-14: Prototype tenant generator implemented (load profiles + seq len distribution). Early runs show p99 divergence when capacity mask reduced to 40% — good signal for kernel selection issues.

2025-07-18: Decided to prioritize fast-mode first to unblock pipeline integration. Trade-off: fast-mode uses lighter-weight approximations for KV cache behavior; will quantify mismatch with fidelity runs later.

2025-07-21: Drafted delta-compatibility report format and sample remediation hints (e.g., reduce batch_size for Dedicated, enable local KMS caching for Private). Pushed RFC to repo: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cht-rfc
2025-07-25: Initial runner integrated into CI as smoke-check; failing test discovered due to suppressed telemetry in private lab — added agent-based collection stub to tasks.
decisions: Adopt hypothesis template approach rather than ad-hoc env scripts to make tests reproducible and shareable.
Two-mode execution: fast/approximate (short feedback loop) and fidelity (longer, more accurate). Start with fast mode to reduce blocker risk for release pipelines.
Report will be both human readable (Console link) and machine-readable (JSON) so pipelines can gate on specific fields.
For Private environments where outgoing telemetry is restricted, use an agent-based collection mechanism that ships summaries into an internal staging store validated by security.
review_feedback: Rafael Gomez (runtime): Recommend adding kernel-availability as first-class hypothesis dimension; some regressions only surface when a specific kernel path is unavailable.
Aisha Patel (infra): Suggest capacity masks include ephemeral burst windows to model autoscaling behavior in Dedicated pools.
Elena Park (security): Agent collection for Private must support local buffering and strict PII redaction; add checklist to security review.
Product (Ruth Becker): Ensure Console UX surfaces remediation steps and impact estimate so SREs can make informed go/no-go decisions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fast-mode false negatives might allow regressions to reach canary. Mitigation: require periodic fidelity sweeps and block high-impact rollouts without recent fidelity verification.
Risk: Private environments may refuse any telemetry. Mitigation: provide an offline report exporter that customers can run and upload; document minimal data needed for checks.
Risk: Simulation complexity grows unwieldy. Mitigation: start with curated hypothesis templates and expand based on incident-driven needs.
Risk: CI runtime cost for fidelity runs. Mitigation: cap fidelity jobs and run them on demand or scheduled windows; use smart sampling of change delta to decide when fidelity is required.
